title: Memes for 2030
lines: Memes for 2030 explores ten ideas that could give technological change a human direction.
Its memes are portable cultural propositions, rather than jokes or predictions of guaranteed virality.
The book connects each phrase with an unmet need, possible practices, and dangers of corruption.
Maintenance, community, freedom, and public responsibility become questions about what societies choose to admire.
Readers gain material for making ideas consequential, instead of merely making them visible.

title: A phrase needs a practice
lines: The book treats a memorable phrase as a beginning, rather than a completed cultural change.
Maintenance Is Heroism asks what happens when care and repair receive visible status.
A bridge inspection, a software patch, and sustained care become parts of one moral reversal.
The chapter also asks when preserving an institution merely protects something that should change.
Each candidate idea is therefore developed through practices and its own possible corruption.

title: Freedom includes chosen absence
lines: Unavailability Is Freedom names the difference between useful connection and permanent obligation to respond.
The book explores how that principle could alter expectations, products, and institutional rules.
Its discussion of fame similarly connects attention with disclosure, repair, restraint, and succession.
These ideas are cultural proposals, not measured predictions about which slogan will succeed.
Their ethical value must remain distinct from their ability to spread.

title: Read beyond the ten phrases
lines: Begin with the introduction on how private discomfort can acquire shared public language.
Then choose a chapter whose tension appears in your own work or community.
Follow its emotional need, possible practices, and warnings together.
Memes for 2030 offers ten open prototypes for cultural imagination rather than a marketing formula.
Read it to explore which ideas deserve a public life and what that life would require.
